before.description_long:
Notion AI is the artificial-intelligence layer inside Notion, the document and database workspace. It lives directly in your pages, so instead of switching to a separate chatbot you summon it where your notes, wikis and project databases already are.

The current release is Notion 3.8, shipped October 13, 2026, under the theme 'Context for your agents'. It lets outside AI agents connect into a workspace through MCP with admin controls, adds a Skills API that syncs Skills written in Notion out to assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude, brings in several new models from vendors including OpenAI and Anthropic, and lets Business and Enterprise workspaces connect a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan to cover AI usage inside Notion.

The prior 3.7 release (September 2026) had added an agent Skills system with a skills library, the ability to export Skills to external tools such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Grok, Custom Agents that can call sub-agents, a Notion Agents iOS app, and a redesigned model picker letting workspace owners choose which models are available to the built-in Notion Agent versus Custom Agents. The 3.6 release before that (July 2026) introduced orchestration of External Agents such as Claude and Cursor from shared boards, AI-generated interactive HTML blocks, reading and writing Microsoft Office files (PPTX, XLSX, DOCX) and Outlook, AI Meeting Notes with speaker identification, Enterprise Search across connected apps, and a Research Mode.

Day to day the AI can draft and rewrite text, translate, summarize long pages, fill and query databases, answer questions across your whole workspace, and run multi-step agent tasks. Custom Agents you build yourself are billed on a credit system, free to try and then $10 per 1,000 monthly Notion credits, and their activity can be tracked through audit logging on higher plans.

Pricing has four tiers. Free is $0 per member per month but only includes a capped trial of Notion AI, not ongoing access. Plus is $10 per seat per month billed annually (about $12 per seat per month if billed monthly) and also only includes the AI trial. Business is $20 per seat per month billed annually (about $24 per seat per month if billed monthly) and is the cheapest plan with full, ongoing AI, including the Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search. Enterprise is custom-priced and adds zero data retention with LLM providers. Notion AI is not sold as a separate add-on; it is bundled into the Business and Enterprise seat price, with Custom Agent credits as an extra variable cost, and Business and Enterprise users can now also connect a ChatGPT Plus or Pro plan to help pay for usage.

The main catch is that ongoing AI access sits behind the Business plan. Free and Plus users only get a capped AI trial, so casual users who expect free or cheap AI on their existing workspace will hit a wall quickly. Custom Agent credits are an added, usage-based cost on top of seat pricing, and some higher-end features such as audit logging are reserved for upper tiers.

Notion AI makes most sense for teams already running their knowledge base, docs and projects in Notion who want AI in the same place and are on or willing to move to the Business tier. Solo note-takers on the free or Plus plan will find the AI too limited to rely on day to day.

before.description: Canva AI 2.0 is the conversational core of Canva's Magic Studio, announced at Canva Create 2026 as a research preview that is rolling out over the following weeks: you describe a design in text or voice and it returns an editable layout, built on Canva's own Design Model.
before.description_long:
Canva AI is the AI layer inside Canva, the browser-based design platform used for social posts, presentations, documents, and marketing assets. Rather than a single feature, it is now a conversational assistant that sits on top of the whole editor.

Canva AI 2.0, unveiled at Canva Create 2026, recasts Canva as a conversational, agentic assistant that Canva positions as part of a broader 'Creative Operating System,' adding connectors, scheduling, web research, brand intelligence, Sheets AI, and Canva Code 2.0. It launched as a research preview and is rolling out to accounts over the following weeks. It runs on the Canva Design Model, a design-specific foundation model, and introduces Magic Layers, which splits an AI-generated poster back into separate, editable layers; Magic Layers is also available inside ChatGPT and Gemini.

Magic Studio bundles the rest: Magic Design for templates, Dream Lab for image generation with style transfer, Magic Write for copy, Canva Sheets and Magic Charts for data-to-visualization plus Magic Insights, and Magic Switch, which now does AI-driven layout redesign rather than simple resizing. The assistant also keeps persistent memory and stays aware of your brand assets.

Canva offers a free plan alongside paid Pro and Business tiers and a custom-priced Enterprise tier. Canva localizes pricing by region, and exact monthly or annual dollar figures for Pro and Business could not be confirmed from a direct read of Canva's pricing page at the time of this review, so check canva.com/pricing for current rates in your country.

The limits are worth knowing. The free plan's AI credit allowance is limited, though the exact cap isn't published; generation quality still varies and often needs manual cleanup; the conversational assistant is best for common formats rather than highly bespoke design work; and because Canva AI 2.0 is a rolling research-preview release, some features may not yet be available on every account.

It suits solo creators, small marketing teams, social media managers, and non-designers who want good-looking, on-brand assets fast without learning a professional design tool.

before.description_long:
Perplexity is a conversational search tool that answers questions with cited, up-to-date sources instead of a list of links. It sits somewhere between a chatbot and a search engine, and it has leaned hard into research and agentic work.

The headline feature is Advanced Deep Research. It runs agentically inside Perplexity's Computer assistant, asks clarifying questions before it starts, accepts follow-ups mid-run, and shows live source and progress tracking.

Beyond research, Perplexity gives you multi-model access to systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and other vendors, plus the Comet browser for AI-assisted browsing.

Pricing is tiered. Free costs $0 a month. Pro costs $20 a month or $200 a year billed annually, and includes 4,000 bonus Computer credits; Perplexity's own pricing page shows the annual plan's per-month equivalent as $17. Max costs $200 a month or $2,000 a year billed annually, shown as an annual-equivalent $167 a month, and includes 10,000 monthly Computer credits plus 35,000 bonus credits. Enterprise Pro costs $40 per seat per month or $400 per seat per year (education/nonprofit pricing is lower), and Enterprise Max costs $325 per seat per month or $3,250 per seat per year. An Education Pro plan is available at $10 a month with SheerID student verification.

The limitations are worth knowing. Like any AI system it can still misread or over-trust weak sources, so citations need checking. The free tier is limited for frequent use, and agentic Computer work is metered by a monthly credit budget that heavy users can exhaust. Juggling multiple models also adds a learning curve for some users.

Perplexity is a strong pick if you do a lot of source-backed research, want agentic Deep Research, or like having access to several AI models in one subscription. Casual users who just need a few answers a day can stay on Free, while heavier users can choose either monthly or annual billing on Pro or Max.

ElevenLabs is a voice-focused AI company best known for realistic text-to-speech and voice cloning. Beyond TTS it now spans audiobooks, music generation and voice agents, making it one of the more complete audio stacks available to developers and creators.

The current flagship models are Eleven v4 and Eleven v4 Turbo, released September 28, 2026. Both support more than 90 languages and are available across ElevenAgents, ElevenCreative and the ElevenAPI. Eleven v4 Turbo is the low-latency variant built for voice agents, with around 100ms median inference latency and roughly 150ms median time to first speech over WebSocket. The previous generation, Eleven v3, reached general availability in February 2026 and remains available but has been superseded by v4 for most use cases.

Core capabilities include high-quality multilingual TTS, instant voice cloning from about 10 seconds of audio, professional studio-grade cloning, real-time conversational agents powered by Eleven v4 Turbo, music generation, and an API with its own subscription tiers for production use.

There is a free plan with 10,000 credits per month, up to 3 Studio projects and no credit rollover, covering TTS, speech-to-text, sound effects, voice design, music and image generation. Paid tiers are billed monthly or annually (annual billing gives two months free): Starter is $6/mo ($5/mo billed annually) with commercial rights and instant cloning; Creator is $22/mo ($18.33/mo billed annually) with professional cloning, sometimes promoted at a discounted first-month rate; Pro is $99/mo ($82.50/mo billed annually); Scale is $299/mo ($249.17/mo billed annually, 3 seats); and Business is $990/mo ($825/mo billed annually, 10 seats). Custom Enterprise pricing is also available.

The main limitations are credit-based usage that can run out quickly on higher-volume work, no commercial rights or required attribution on the free plan, and costs that climb fast once you need many hours of audio or several seats. Voice cloning also raises consent and misuse concerns you have to manage yourself.

ElevenLabs suits creators, studios and developers who need natural-sounding voices in many languages, teams building voice agents, and anyone producing audiobooks or narration at scale.

before.description_long:
Zapier is a cloud automation service that links the apps you already use so data and tasks move between them without manual copy-paste. You build workflows called Zaps, which run on triggers and actions, and you can also create Tables, Interfaces, and Chatbots inside the same account.

The platform has shifted toward AI. Zapier Copilot, listed in Beta on every plan, turns plain-language descriptions into working Zaps, Tables, Interfaces, Chatbots, and Agents. Zapier Agents are AI teammates that can take action without waiting for a trigger, and Zapier MCP exposes Zapier's triggers and actions to outside models such as Claude and GPT, with each MCP tool call drawing from the plan's task quota.

Integration coverage stands at 9,000+ apps, on top of multi-step Zaps, filters, paths, formatting, and webhooks, plus the Tables and Interfaces tools that push Zapier closer to a lightweight app builder than a simple connector.

Pricing is freemium. The Free plan is $0/month with 100 tasks per month, unlimited two-step Zaps, Tables, and Forms, and a limited-message version of Copilot. Professional starts at $19.99/month billed annually (or $29.99/month billed monthly), with 750 tasks that scale up to 2 million tasks. Team starts at $69/month billed annually (or $103.50/month billed monthly) for 25 users with 2,000 tasks at entry. Enterprise pricing is custom. The AI products are billed separately: Agents (a free tier with 400 activities/month, a Pro tier at $33.33/month billed annually, and custom Enterprise pricing) and Chatbots (a free tier with 2 bots, a Pro tier at $13.33/month billed annually, an Advanced tier at $66.67/month billed annually, and custom pricing).

The main limitation is cost at scale: tasks are metered, and busy workflows or the separately billed AI products can add up quickly. Advanced logic can get fiddly, and autonomous Agents and Copilot output still benefit from human review before you rely on them unattended.

Zapier fits teams and solo operators who want to automate across many SaaS tools without code, and who want AI to draft and maintain those automations. If you need only one or two heavy, high-volume pipelines, a cheaper task model elsewhere may serve you better.

before.description_long:
Devin Desktop, formerly known as Windsurf, is an AI-native code editor built by Cognition. It combines an autocomplete engine (Tab), inline edits, and autonomous coding agents inside a VS Code-style workspace. Windsurf for JetBrains continues to be offered under the original Windsurf name.

The product was renamed from Windsurf to Devin Desktop on June 2, 2026, after Cognition and Windsurf came together. windsurf.com and codeium.com/windsurf now redirect to devin.ai/desktop. The in-editor agent picker currently lists several selectable agents, including Devin Local, Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode and Cascade, so the original Cascade agent is still available rather than retired.

On the model side, SWE-2 is the current in-house model, released September 10, 2026, replacing the earlier SWE-1.6. Paid tiers also unlock access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceXAI, and leading open-source models, along with Devin Cloud agents for longer background tasks and Devin Review for automated code review.

Pricing runs on daily and weekly quotas rather than the older credit system. Free is $0 per month with a light agent quota, limited model access, and unlimited Tab completions and inline edits. Pro is $20 per month with increased quotas, full model access, Devin Cloud agents, up to 10 concurrent sessions, and free use of SWE-2 through October 16, 2026 as a limited-time offer. Max is $200 per month with significantly higher quotas. Teams costs $80 per month as a base plus $40 per month per developer seat for up to 200 users, and Enterprise pricing is custom with SSO and VPC deployment.

The main caveats are churn and lock-in: the rebrand from Windsurf to Devin Desktop, and the move from credits to quotas, mean workflows and limits have shifted within the same year. Heavy agent use can burn through quotas quickly, and the free access to SWE-2 on Pro is time-limited rather than permanent. Much of the product's value now sits behind the Devin ecosystem.

It suits developers who want an agent-first editor with strong autocomplete and are comfortable working inside the Cognition/Devin ecosystem. Anyone still looking for the original Windsurf branding or credit-based pricing should know those have changed, though Windsurf branding persists in the JetBrains plugin.

before.description: Replit Agent 4 runs parallel agents that build authentication, database, backend, and frontend components simultaneously, and includes a Security Agent that scans codebases for vulnerabilities.
before.description_long:
Replit is a browser-based development platform that combines a cloud IDE, AI coding agent, and instant deployment into a single environment. No local setup is required — users write, run, and ship code entirely in the browser, making it accessible for beginners and fast for prototyping.

The current generation, Agent 4, repositions Replit from an AI coding agent toward a broader creative agent, described by Replit as turning ideas into apps, designs, slides, and more, with design variants generated on an infinite canvas as a headline feature.

Agent 4 introduces multi-task parallelism: instead of building an app sequentially, it spins up parallel agents that handle authentication, database setup, backend logic, and frontend code at the same time, with progress visible in a dedicated panel. The Security Agent performs codebase scanning at three levels: a free dependency and static code analysis pass, a white-box scan, and a combined white-box plus black-box scan; Replit has not published scan duration figures.

Pricing, read from replit.com/pricing, has no listed $0 account tier. Core costs $20/month billed monthly, or $18/month billed annually, and includes $20 in monthly credits plus a Free Mode allowance of up to 30 hours of chat and 60 projects. Pro costs $100/month billed monthly, or $90/month billed annually, includes $100 in credits, 10 parallel agents, up to 15 collaborators and 50 viewers, and 28-day database rollback. Enterprise pricing is custom and adds SSO/SAML, single-tenant environments, and static outbound IPs.

before.description_long:
Seedance 2.0 is an AI video generation model developed by ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. Released February 12, 2026, it is one of the most capable open-access video generation models available, notable for accepting a wide range of input modalities and for its Temporal Anchor technology that addresses character consistency across frames.

Seedance 2.0 accepts up to 12 assets per generation request, spanning text prompts, reference images, audio tracks, and existing video clips. This multimodal input capability allows creators to anchor a generation with visual references, add a specific audio track, and direct the narrative with text — all in a single request. Few competing video generation models support this breadth of input types simultaneously.

Temporal Anchor is the key technical differentiator in Seedance 2.0. It is a framework for maintaining consistent character appearance, object identity, and scene continuity across the full length of a generated clip. Earlier video generation models suffered from morphing and flickering — where a character's face or an object's appearance would change subtly or abruptly between frames. Temporal Anchor eliminates this, enabling consistent characters across clips up to 60 seconds in length.

Output is 1080p native, with no upscaling required. Generation speed is 30–40% faster than Seedance 1.0, making the model more practical for iterative production workflows. The free tier includes commercial rights and outputs without watermarks — a significant advantage over competitors that restrict commercial use to paid plans.

Seedance 2.0 is integrated into Krea AI, HeyGen, and ComfyUI, allowing users to access its capabilities within those platforms' own workflows and interfaces without managing a separate API integration.

Seedance 2.0 is best for video creators, marketers, and developers who need consistent-character video generation at 1080p with no watermark and commercial rights included at no cost, and for teams that use Krea AI, HeyGen, or ComfyUI in their existing workflows.

Kling AI is a video generation platform built by the Chinese company Kuaishou. You describe a scene in text, or feed it a still image, and it animates a short cinematic clip. Over the past two years it has grown from an experimental demo into one of the most widely used AI video tools.

Kling 4.0 Flash entered early access on September 28, 2026, available to Ultra yearly subscribers, generating clips of up to 20 seconds at 720p with 8-bit SDR. Kling's own release note said the full Kling 4.0 model would launch in October 2026; by mid-October, secondary reports suggested it had rolled out more broadly, but this could not be confirmed directly on Kling's own site at the time of writing. Kling AI uses a tiered, credit-based subscription model, with separate plans such as Standard, Pro, Premier and Ultra that unlock larger monthly credit allowances, and annual billing available at a discount on some tiers. Specific current pricing for Kling 4.0 and Flash has not been published, and the previously published rates for the 3.0-era plans could not be reconfirmed at the time of this review.

The main limitations right now are the lack of published pricing for the new model, uncertainty about exactly when the full 4.0 model became generally available, inconsistent reporting across sources about which resolutions (including 4K) are actually live versus still pending, and the fact that several headline features, including 10-bit HDR and the roughly two-minute video extension, are announced but not yet available. Kling 4.0 Flash early access is also gated behind an Ultra-tier yearly subscription.

Kling suits creators, marketers and video editors who want high-quality short clips for social content, ads or B-roll, and who are comfortable working shot by shot while Kuaishou finishes rolling out the newest model's full feature set.

before.description_long:
GitHub Copilot started as an in-editor autocomplete tool, but the current product is a full multi-model coding platform. It lives inside your editor, in the terminal, in a desktop app, and on GitHub itself, handling code completion, chat, an agent mode that edits across files, cloud agents that work on tasks asynchronously, and automated code review.

GitHub has repositioned Copilot around a new desktop app pitched as taking issues all the way to merge, and billing now runs on consumption-based GitHub AI Credits rather than flat request units. Paid plans include both a base monthly credit allowance and an optional flex allowance, and higher tiers can now delegate work to third-party coding agents such as Claude by Anthropic and OpenAI Codex, currently in preview.

The core capabilities are agent mode, cloud agents, chat, code review, a CLI, and the ability to pick from models across multiple vendors including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI, Microsoft and Moonshot. Inline code completions and Next Edit suggestions stay included on every plan and do not draw down your AI Credits allowance.

On pricing, individuals can choose Free at $0 per month (about 2,000 inline suggestions, limited chat and agent usage, no code review or cloud agents), Pro at $10 per month in base credits plus $5 per month in flex credits for $15 per month total (1,500 AI Credits, unlimited inline suggestions, code review and cloud agents), Pro+ at $39 per month base plus $31 per month flex for $70 per month total (3,900 plus 3,100 credits, adds delegation to third-party coding agents), or Max at $100 per month base plus $100 per month flex for $200 per month total (10,000 plus 10,000 credits, priority access to premium models). A separate Copilot Student plan gives verified students their own AI Credits allowance, and verified teachers and maintainers of popular open source projects can get Pro for free. Organizations pick Business at $19 per user per month (1,900 AI Credits per user) or Enterprise at $39 per user per month (3,900 AI Credits per user, requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud).

The main limitation is cost predictability: usage-based AI Credits billing, split into base and flex allotments, means heavy agent, chat or premium-model use can push real monthly cost well past the advertised base price. Admin budgets and spending caps help organizations control this, but teams still need to monitor consumption closely.

Copilot is a strong fit if you already work in GitHub and VS Code, want an agentic assistant rather than plain autocomplete, and value being able to choose from models across different vendors. The free tier is a low-risk way to try it, while Pro+ and Max suit heavier users who want premium models and third-party agent delegation.

before.description: Lovable is an agentic no-code platform that turns plain-language prompts into working web apps. It builds autonomously through a default Agent/Build mode, with Plan Mode for previewing changes and automatic subagents handling parallel research and review work, all metered by a unified credit system.
before.description_long:
Lovable lets you describe an app in everyday language and have it built for you, including the interface, logic, and a managed backend. It is aimed at founders, product people, and developers who want to go from idea to a deployable app without writing everything by hand.

The product runs on a fully agentic, credit-based model rather than a versioned release cycle. Agent Mode (also called Build mode) is the default and runs autonomously: it reads your codebase, searches the web, debugs, generates images, and validates its own output. Plan Mode lets you preview intended changes before any code is written, now with diffs and revision history, and Lovable also runs automatic, read-only subagents that handle research and review work in parallel. As of late 2026, builds can run for extended periods per message under a '/goal' mode, and in-app AI features can use Anthropic's Claude models without you supplying your own API key.

On capabilities, the backend is branded Lovable Cloud, a managed layer built on Supabase under the hood, with Lovable AI handling in-app AI features. You get database, auth, and hosting without wiring raw services yourself. Workspace-private projects are included even on the free plan, while code editing, code download, and custom domains are reserved for paid tiers.

Pricing is credit-based across both building and running apps. Free is $0/mo with 5 build credits per day (up to about 30/month), 20 Cloud credits per month, and 4 in-app AI credits per month. Pro is $25/mo billed monthly, or $21/mo billed annually ($250/year) at the 100-credit tier, scaling up to roughly $2,250/mo for 10,000 credits, and adds code editing, code download, and custom domains, with top-ups available at $15 per 50 credits. Business is $50/mo billed monthly, or $42/mo billed annually ($500/year) at the 100-credit tier, scaling up to roughly $4,300/mo, and adds SSO, role-based access, the Lovable API, internal publishing, and opt-out of data training by default, with top-ups at $30 per 50 credits. Enterprise pricing is custom and quote-based, with SCIM, audit logs, publishing and sharing controls, and EU inference options.

The main limitation is the credit model itself: because credits cover building, deployed-app runtime, and in-app AI, costs can be hard to predict on active projects, and the free tier runs out quickly. Autonomous generation is fast but still needs review, and heavy customization eventually pushes you into editing code directly.

Choose Lovable if you want an AI agent to do most of the building and you are comfortable steering it, and budget for credit consumption if your app is more than a prototype.
